AI SITE-INSPECTION REPORTING

From site visit to approved client report, with every statement traceable.

Inspectors capture photos, voice notes and typed observations on their phones. SiteReport turns them into a structured draft. A named reviewer checks each point against its evidence, approves a version, and downloads the report.

    Working in this demo

    • AI structures a free-text note into findings (live, or a labelled replay).
    • Every source quote is checked against the note automatically.
    • A missing location blocks approval until a person fills it in.
    • A named approval freezes the version, with a content fingerprint.
    • The Word report and JSON snapshot come from that frozen version.

    Still to prove at scale

    • Voice transcription and photo upload on real phones.
    • Many firms at once, each fully isolated, under load.
    • Accuracy on real Nigerian English and Pidgin recordings.
    • Restoring both records and files after a failure.
    • Real reports from real firms in a pilot.

    THE PROBLEM

    Site evidence is scattered. The report shouldn’t be.

    After every visit, photos sit in a gallery, notes in chat and measurements in memory. Someone spends the evening matching them up. SiteReport keeps each observation together and turns the lot into one draft that a person approves.

    AI DRAFT

    Paste a site note. Watch it become structured findings.

    This calls Claude with the rules from the build plan: nothing is guessed, missing values stay empty, and every finding needs a quote from your note. Your note is sent to Claude for this request only, and this page stores nothing.

    The rules the AI must follow

    Use only what the note says. Anything not stated is null. Keep measurements in the original wording and say who measured. Keep suspected issues worded as suspected. Never turn “not inspected” into “no defects”. No diagnosis, certification or code judgments. Every finding needs a quote copied from the note, and the page checks that the quote really exists.

      THE SIX STAGES

      Watch a site visit become a reviewed report.

      An animated preview of the six stages, built from the product plan. It is not a screen recording of finished software. Pick a stage or let it play.

        One workflow, four steps

        The inspector supplies the engineering judgment. The software preserves and organizes it.

        01

        Capture

        One observation at a time: location, photos, a short voice or typed note, and any stated action.

        02

        Draft

        Voice is transcribed and facts are extracted into a strict schema. Missing values stay empty, never guessed.

        03

        Review

        Findings sit beside their photos and source note. Unclear points are flagged for the reviewer.

        04

        Approve and export

        An explicit, recorded approval freezes a version. Word and PDF come from that same version.

        BUILT TO SCALE · PLAN

        It works today. Here is what it takes to run it for many firms.

        Each site visit is one independent background job, and every company’s data is kept apart. Adding firms means running more of the same job, not building a different product. What still has to be proven is volume, reliability and accuracy on real material. That is the work extra cloud capacity would pay for.

        01

        One visit, one job

        Processing runs in the background. A retry rebuilds the draft from scratch, so a failed run never duplicates or loses work.

        02

        One bad note can’t sink a visit

        If one observation fails, the rest still process and the reviewer gets a clear placeholder to fill in by hand.

        03

        Isolated by design

        A company id on every table with row-level security, and approved versions that cannot be edited afterwards.

        04

        Replaceable AI provider

        The model call sits behind one function, so moving between providers does not touch the schema, the checks or the review flow.

        Planned architecture on Azure

        Planned, not deployed The pilot plan uses Next.js, Supabase, Trigger.dev and Vercel. This is the proposed mapping for scale. The AI step in this demo runs on Claude.

        What extra capacity would fund

        A

        Evaluation on real material

        Run 30 complete visit packets, 10 of them held out, through transcription and extraction, including Nigerian English and Pidgin recordings. Target: at least 95% precision and recall on labelled facts. A target, not a result.

        B

        Load and isolation tests

        Deliberate cross-company access attempts, double clicks on Generate, provider timeouts and failed uploads. Targets: every attempt rejected, and at least 95% of jobs finish with no developer help.

        C

        Recovery, actually rehearsed

        Restore both the database records and the real photo and audio files after a drill, within a recovery target agreed in advance.

        D

        A controlled pilot

        Two or three firms, about ten real reports each, measuring time saved, correction effort, job reliability and processing cost.

        TECHNOLOGY

        Five checks behind every draft.

        SiteReport isn’t a chatbot that writes a report. It structures what was observed and checks its own work before a person sees it.

        01

        Transcribe

        Voice notes become text, kept with the original audio.

        02

        Extract

        Findings must fit a strict schema. Anything that doesn’t is rejected and retried.

        03

        Verify

        Each finding’s source quote must exist in the input, or it goes to the reviewer.

        04

        Flag

        Missing locations, vague wording and suspected issues are marked, never resolved by guessing.

        05

        Freeze

        Approval locks an exact version. Exports come only from that snapshot.

        SECURITY

        Client site data stays protected.

        These are the pilot’s design requirements. Each is tested before any firm uses the product with real work.

        Company isolation

        Enforced in the database, so one firm can’t see another’s records.

        Private files

        Photos and audio sit in private storage, shared only through short-lived links.

        Immutable approvals

        Approved versions can’t be edited. Corrections create a new draft.

        Role-based approval

        Only reviewers and admins can approve a report.

        Audit trail

        Processing and approval events are logged.

        Built around honesty about evidence

        • Every material statement links to a source or is marked as reviewer entered.
        • “Not inspected” is never turned into “no defects found”.
        • Measurements keep their original wording beside any parsed value.
        • No weather, completion percentages, grades or signatures are invented.
        • Approval refers to the exact content version the reviewer saw.
        • Later corrections create a new draft that needs approval again.
        • Company data is isolated, files are private, and uploads show “Uploaded” only once confirmed.
        • No diagnosis, certification or code-compliance judgments.

        Questions firms ask

        Does the AI make engineering judgments?

        No. It structures what the inspector said and photographed. It does not diagnose, grade severity, certify, or judge code compliance. A named reviewer approves every report.

        What if the AI gets something wrong?

        Each finding sits beside its photos and source note, and unclear points are flagged. The reviewer can edit anything. If a correction is needed after approval, it creates a new draft that must be approved again.

        Does it work with Nigerian accents and Pidgin?

        That has to be tested, not assumed. The pilot plan compares transcription options on real recordings from real sites before choosing one.

        What about sites with poor connectivity?

        Offline capture is deliberately deferred. The pilot will show whether connectivity blocks real visits, and if it does, offline capture becomes its own milestone.

        Is our data kept separate from other firms?

        That is a design requirement: company data is isolated, files are private, and isolation is tested before any pilot. This preview page stores nothing.
